proposals.mechanism: no_closure_at_velar: tongue body reaches 5.5-8.5 cm but narrows only to 0.20 cm2 (stroke 0.95 of the 1.2 cm bore radius leaves ~0.25 cm radius = 0.196 cm2).
proposals.principle: A stop needs an articulator that reaches its place and seals the bore; cam lift past the 1.2 cm bore radius squeezes the tube shut.
proposals.hypothesis: Raising stroke from 0.95 to 1.3 (> 1.2 bore radius) lets the pad seal (<0.05 cm2) at the velar place with the lips and pharynx open (>1 cm2). No place change can fix it since sealing depends only on stroke; this is the cheapest rung.
risks: ih: tighter maximum lift means the same control travel spans more depth, raising noise sensitivity of high-front vowels; System 1 re-searches tongue_height and the 0.20 cm2 postures stay reachable at partial lift.
proposals.result: not kept (another proposal gained more): gained k, lost none; costs $0.00, 50 machine min

proposals.mechanism: no_closure_at_lips (lips stop at 3.00 cm2) and f2_floor_too_high for uw/uh/ao (with F1 near target, F2 floors 1747/1147/1126 Hz vs targets 870/1020/840).
proposals.principle: Lip opening is a velocity maximum of every formant: closing and protruding the lips lowers F1, F2, F3; a longer lip tube lowers all formants together. A stop at the lips needs a lip seal.
proposals.hypothesis: jaw_lips has no value that closes below 2.5 cm2 or protrudes, so a params move cannot help. round_lips gives 0-6.6 cm2 (seal for /p/) and up to 1.6 cm protrusion (lip tube 2.6 cm, tract to 16.1 cm) plus small rounded opening, dropping F2 toward 870-1020 Hz for back rounded vowels. Retractable protrusion avoids the long_cast penalty on aa F1 (ceiling 854 would fall ~708 < 730 target) and iy F2.
risks: ae: max opening 6.6 vs 6.9 cm2 now; slight F1 ceiling drop, but at zero protrusion the tract length is unchanged (14.5 cm) and current aa/ae solutions are within range.
iy: lip tube unchanged at zero protrusion, so F2 2290 remains reachable.

proposals.mechanism: no_closure_at_alveolar: no articulator reaches 0-1.5 cm behind the teeth (tongue pad starts at 3.25, rail_start min 2.5); also no_closure_at_velar (stroke 0.95 < 1.2); f3_floor_too_high for er (lowest F3 2769 vs 1690) needs simultaneous constrictions.
proposals.principle: A stop needs an articulator that reaches its place and seals; a very low F3 needs constrictions near several F3 velocity maxima at once.
proposals.hypothesis: cam_tongue's rail_start range [2.5,4] can never reach the alveolar place, so a swap is required. tip_tongue adds a tip blade sliding 0.3-5 cm behind the teeth that seals the full bore (/t/), while its body pad at stroke 1.3 seals the velar place (/k/). Two independent constrictions (tip under the palate + body pad toward the pharynx) give /er/ a chance to pull F3 down, especially together with round_lips.
risks: eh: body pad keeps same rail (3.25-10.25) so vowel postures remain; tip can be parked retracted. Higher stroke raises noise sensitivity but System 1 refits height.
proposals.result: not kept (another proposal gained more): gained k, t, uh, uw, lost none; costs $12.00, 76 machine min

iterations.notes: If proposals 2 and 3 are combined, they need 6 servos (all 6 controller channels). My estimated shopping list is 2 pushrod kits ($8) and 2 extra servos ($16), about $24 in total, with 3 days of lead time and 133 machine minutes, all within the limits. I rejected long_cast because a longer tract would lower the F1 ceiling below the /ɑ/ target (730 Hz) and also lower F2 for /i/. I avoided pneumatic_tongue because its valve manifold cannot be bought.
